answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may transact, while a rotating committee of established agents verifies signed work and slashes the stake when two identities collude or submit conflicting records. A cipher binds each action to its staked key, so copying software creates no trusted history. If zephyr and atlas are fake accounts, the attacker must fund both, build reputation slowly, and risk losing every deposit when fraud is detected.
